Papagiannis''' ([[Greek language|Greek]]: Γιώργος Παπαγιάννης; born July 3, 1997), is a Greek professional [[basketball]] player for [[Anadolu Efes S.K.|Anadolu Efes]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL) and the [[EuroLeague]]. Born in [[Marousi]], [[Attica]], Greece, he is a 7 ft 2 {{3/4}} in (2.20 m)[http://www.euroleague.net/competition/players/showplayer?pcode=005844 PAPAGIANNIS, GEORGIOS HEIGHT: 2.20.] tall [[center (basketball)|center]], with a 7 ft 6 in (2.29 m) [[wingspan]].{{cite web|title=7 Foot Greek Hoops Phenom Georgios Papagiannis is Coming to America|url=http://thehoopdoctors.com/2013/09/7-foot-greek-hoops-phenom-georgios-papagiannis-is-coming-to-america/|work=TheHoopDoctors.com|date=September 23, 2013|access-date=September 23, 2013}} An [[All-Euroleague Second Team|All-EuroLeague Second Team]] selection in [[2021–22 EuroLeague|2022]], Papagiannis is a member of the senior [[Greek national basketball team|National Team of Greece]]. ==Early life== Papagiannis was born in [[Marousi]], a northern suburb of [[Athens]], [[Greece]], and spent his early years in [[Megara]], in the [[West Attica|western region of Athens]]. Papagiannis played at the [[Jordan Brand Classic]] International Game in 2013.{{cite web|title=2013 Jordan Brand Classic International Game|url=http://jordanbrandclassic.com/2012/12/2013-jordan-brand-classic-international-game/|work=JordanBrandClassic.com|date=March 3, 2013|access-date=March 3, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160910003138/http://jordanbrandclassic.com/2012/12/2013-jordan-brand-classic-international-game/|archive-date=September 10, 2016|url-status=dead}} He announced that he was committing to [[Westtown School]] in [[West Chester, Pennsylvania]], in May 2013. He then attended school and played basketball at Westtown, during the 2013–14 academic school year and basketball season, as a high school junior.{{cite web|first=Joseph|last=Santoliquito|title=Westtown's Georgios Papagiannis enters high school basketball with NBA possibilities|url=http://www.maxpreps.com/news/-vu2vYEFc0K7bGLQqcIg_w/westtowns-georgios-papagiannis-enters-high-school-basketball-with-nba-possibilities.htm|work=MaxPreps.com|date=October 29, 2013|access-date=October 29, 2013}} After his junior year of high school in the United States, he transferred to the [[American Community Schools|American School]] in [[Athens, Greece]], for his senior year of high school. ==Professional career== ===Peristeri (2012–2013)=== Papagiannis made his senior men's club debut with [[Peristeri BC|Peristeri]] on January 5, 2012, at the age of 14, in a [[Greek Basket League]] 2011–12 season game against [[Panathinaikos BC|Panathinaikos]].{{cite web|title=ESAKE.gr Day 11|url=http://www.esake.gr/el/action/EsakegameView?idgame=41A19B61&mode=2|work=Esake.gr|access-date=June 9, 2012|language=el}} He became the youngest player to ever play in the modern era of the Greek Basket League (since the league first became fully [[professional sports|professional]], under the organization of [[HEBA]], starting with the 1992–93 season).{{cite web|title=Real Madrid set sights on Georgios Papagiannis|url=http://thehoop.blogspot.mx/2012/06/real-madrid-set-sights-on-georgios.html|work=TheHoop.blogspot.mx|date=June 9, 2012|access-date=June 9, 2012}}{{cite web|script-title=el:Παπαγιάννης ο "Βενιαμίν" της Α1|url=http://www.real.gr/DefaultArthro.aspx?page=arthro&id=115855&catID=14|work=Real.gr|date=January 6, 2012|access-date=January 6, 2012|language=el}} He also spent the entire 2012–13 season with Peristeri.{{cite web|title=Giorgos Papagiannis career stats & achievements|url=http://widgets.baskethotel.com/site/esake/player/4968203/|work=BasketHotel.com|access-date=June 25, 2014}} ===Panathinaikos (2014–2016)=== On June 25, 2014, Papagiannis signed with [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]] on a multi-year deal, yet there was a player option in the contract, which allowed him to leave Panathinaikos for a US college during the summer of 2015.{{cite web|title=Panathinaikos and Papagiannis reach agreement|url=http://www.paobc.gr/page.ashx?pid=2&aid=24076&lang=2|work=PAOBC.gr|date=June 25, 2014|access-date=June 25, 2014|archive-date=June 29, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140629232639/http://www.paobc.gr/page.ashx?pid=2&aid=24076&lang=2|url-status=dead}} Papagiannis, considered to be one of the biggest young European talent prospects, received scholarship offers from 17 USA colleges, including [[University of Connecticut|UConn]], [[University of Arizona|Arizona]], [[Temple University|Temple]],{{cite web|title=UConn interested in Greek big man Georgios Papagiannis|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/usa/ncaa/150164/uconn-interested-in-greek-big-man-georgios-papagiannis.html|work=Sportando.com|date=January 27, 2015|access-date=January 27, 2015}} [[North Carolina State University|NC State]],{{cite web|first=Matt|last=Hladik|title=Report: 4-Star Center Georgios Papagiannis Won't Play College Basketball, Will Pursue Pro Career In Greece|url=http://thespun.com/pac-12/oregon/report-4-star-center-georgios-papagiannis-wont-play-college-basketball-will-pursue-pro-career-in-greece|work=TheSpun.com|date=July 8, 2015|access-date=July 8, 2015}} [[University of Oregon|Oregon]], [[St. John's University (New York City)|St. John's]], and [[University of Kentucky|Kentucky]].{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Winn|title=Possible Greek import Georgios Papagiannis could be recruiting coup|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2015/06/30/georgios-papagiannis-recruiting-2015-nba-draft-2016-oregon-kentucky-st-johns|work=SI.com|date=July 1, 2015|access-date=July 1, 2015}} On July 8, 2015, it was announced that Papagiannis had chosen to continue playing for Panathinaikos.{{cite web|first=Giorgos|last=Orfanaki|script-title=el:Διάλεξε ΠΑΟ ο Παπαγιάννης|url=http://www.eurohoops.net/el/featured-el/108599/αποφάσισε-παο-ο-παπαγιάννης|work=EuroHoops.net|date=July 8, 2015|access-date=July 8, 2015|language=el}} His Panathinaikos contract included a €500,000 [[euros]] buyout option.{{cite web|first=Aris|last=Barkas|title=Papagiannis flirting with the first round|url=http://www.eurohoops.net/featured/266605/papagiannis-flirting-with-the-first-round|work=EuroHoops.net|date=June 22, 2016|access-date=June 22, 2016}} Papagiannis was a member of the Panathinaikos teams that won both the [[2014–15 Greek Basketball Cup|2015 edition]] and the [[2015–16 Greek Basketball Cup|2016 edition]] of the [[Greek Basketball Cup|Greek Cup]]. He also played in six games with Panathinaikos during the [[2015–16 Euroleague|2015–16 EuroLeague]] season competition, where he averaged 1.5 points and 1.7 rebounds per game, in 5 minutes per game.{{cite web|title=PAPAGIANNIS, GEORGIOS Euroleague 2015-16 STATISTICS|url=http://www.euroleague.net/competition/players/showplayer?pcode=005844&seasoncode=E2015|work=Euroleague.net|access-date=April 19, 2016}} In the 2015–16 Greek League season, he averaged 6.5 points and 2.8 rebounds per game, in 11.5 minutes per game, in 23 games played.{{cite web|title= Σ Γιώργος - Basket League ΣΚΡΑΤΣ 2015-16|url=http://www.esake.gr/el/action/EsakeplayerView?idplayer=00000451&mode=1&idchampionship=|work=Esake.gr|access-date=April 19, 2016|language=el}} ===Sacramento Kings (2016–2018)=== In April 2016, Papagiannis entered the [[2016 NBA draft]],{{cite web|title=Georgios Papagiannis will enter the 2016 NBA Draft|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/usa/nba/197437/georgios-papagiannis-will-enter-the-2016-nba-draft.html|work=Sportando.com|date=April 19, 2016|access-date=April 19, 2016}} and was projected as a mid-to-late second round pick, but he also garnered interest as a late first-round pick.{{cite web|first=Steve|last=Kyler|title=NBA AM: Is Derrick Rose On His Way Out?|url=http://www.basketballinsiders.com/nba-am-is-derrick-rose-on-his-way-out/|work=BasketballInsiders.com|date=June 4, 2016|access-date=June 4, 2016}} However, on June 23, Papagiannis was selected with the 13th overall pick by the [[Phoenix Suns]], becoming the highest drafted Greek player ever. His rights were later traded to the [[Sacramento Kings]] on draft night,{{cite web|title=Kings Announce Draft-Night Trade|url=http://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-announce-draft-night-trade|work=NBA.com|date=June 23, 2016|access-date=November 12, 2016}} and in July, he joined the Kings for the [[2016 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|title=Kings Announce 2016 NBA Summer League Roster|url=http://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-announce-2016-nba-summer-league-roster/|work=NBA.com|date=July 5, 2016|access-date=November 12, 2016}} On July 15, 2016, he signed his rookie scale contract with the Kings.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-sign-papagiannis-richardson-labissiere|title=Kings Sign Papagiannis, Richardson and Labissiere|work=NBA.com|date=July 15, 2016|access-date=July 15, 2016}} On November 5, 2016, he made his NBA debut in a 117–91 loss to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], recording two points and one rebound in six minutes off the bench.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=400899535|title=Kings vs. Bucks – Box Score|work=ESPN.com|date=November 5, 2016|access-date=November 12, 2016}} On March 18, 2017, he had his first double-double with 14 points and 11 rebounds in the Kings' 110–94 loss to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com.au/nba/recap?gameId=400900423|title=Westbrook leads Thunder past Kings without triple-double|work=ESPN.com|date=March 18, 2017|access-date=March 18, 2017}} During his rookie season, he had multiple assignments with the [[Reno Bighorns]] of the [[NBA Development League]].{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/assignments/|title=2016-17 NBA Assignments|work=NBA.com|access-date=November 26, 2016|archive-date=January 26, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170126075350/http://dleague.nba.com/assignments/|url-status=dead}} On February 8, 2018, Papagiannis was waived by the Kings.{{cite tweet|number=961717195804995586|user=ShamsCharania|title=Sources: The Kings are waiving center...|date=8 February 2018}} ===Portland Trail Blazers (2018)=== On March 8, 2018, Papagiannis signed a 10-day contract with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers Sign Georgios Papagiannis To 10-Day Contract|url=http://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-sign-georgios-papagiannis-10-day-contract|website=NBA.com|access-date=March 12, 2018|language=en}} Despite not playing a single game for Portland at the end of his 10-day contract, Papagiannis signed a two-year contract on March 18.[http://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-sign-georgios-papagiannis-through-2018-19 TRAIL BLAZERS SIGN GEORGIOS PAPAGIANNIS THROUGH 2018-19.] He appeared in one game with the Blazers. Papagiannis was waived by the Blazers after the end of the 2018 NBA Summer League.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/mlb/story/_/id/24125874/portland-trail-blazers-waive-center-george-papagiannis |title=George Papagiannis waived by Trail Blazers, planning to sign in Greece |author= |date=July 18, 2018 |website=ESPN |publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures |access-date=August 2, 2018}} === Return to Panathinaikos (2018–2023) === On July 20, 2018, Papagiannis returned to [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]], signing a five-year contract,[http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/8vvlbterd3sbx3qw/panathinaikos-brings-papagiannis-home Panathinaikos brings Papagiannis home.] with the last two years of the contract being team options.[http://www.sport24.gr/Basket/OmadesBasket/A1Panathinaikos/ypegrapse-o-papagiannhs-ston-panathhnaiko-photo.5266396.html Υπέγραψε ο Παπαγιάννης στον Παναθηναϊκό (PHOTO) {{in lang|el}}.] The contract also included an [[NBA]] opt-out option, after the third year of the contract.[https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/715008/papagiannis-signed-with-panathinaikos/ Papagiannis signed with Panathinaikos.] After the departure of [[Ioannis Papapetrou]] in the summer of 2022, Papagiannis was named [[captain (sports)|team captain]] for the first time in his career. During the 2022–2023 campaign, in 33 EuroLeague games, he averaged 8.5 points, 5.7 rebounds and 1.2 blocks in 24 minutes per contest. Additionally, in 34 domestic league matches, he averaged 9.3 points, 6 rebounds, 1.3 assists and 1.2 blocks in 22 minutes per contest. On July 14, 2023, after weeks of stagnant negotiations, Papagiannis informed Panathinaikos that he had rejected their contract renewal proposal and he would be leaving the club after a total of seven seasons together. ===Fenerbahçe (2023–2024)=== On July 15, 2023, Papagiannis signed a two-year deal with Turkish powerhouse [[Fenerbahçe S.K. (basketball)|Fenerbahçe]], under his national team coach [[Dimitrios Itoudis]]. ===AS Monaco (2024–2025)=== Papagiannis spent the 2024–25 campaign with French-based club [[AS Monaco Basket|Monaco]], reaching the [[EuroLeague]] final in Abu Dhabi. ===Anadolu Efes (2025–present)=== On July 16, 2025, Papagiannis signed a three-year (2+1) deal with [[Anadolu Efes S.K.|Anadolu Efes]] of the Turkish [[Basketbol Süper Ligi|Basketball Super League]] (BSL).{{Cite web|url=https://www.anadoluefessk.org/haber/georgios-papagiannis-anadolu-efes-te|title=Georgios Papagiannis Anadolu Efes’te|date=July 16, 2025|website=|publisher=[[Anadolu Efes S.K.|Anadolu Efes]]|language=tr|access-date=July 16, 2025}} ==National team career== ===Greek junior national team=== With the [[Greece men's national under-16 basketball team|Greek Under-16 junior national team]], Papagiannis played at the [[2012 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship]], which he led in blocks per game.{{cite web|title=FIBAEurope.com STATISTICAL LEADERS - PLAYERS Blocked Shots|url=https://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/statistics/p/rpp//tid/291/sid/8814/sp/ALL/ss/BL/srid/ALL/_/2012_U16_European_Championship_Men/player-leaders.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160814151510/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/statistics/p/rpp//tid/291/sid/8814/sp/ALL/ss/BL/srid/ALL/_/2012_U16_European_Championship_Men/player-leaders.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 14, 2016|work=FIBA.com|access-date=April 19, 2016}} He also played with Greece at the 2013 [[TBF International Under-16 Tournament|TBF Under-16 World Cup]] in Sakarya, Turkey, where he helped Greece win the gold medal. He also played at the [[2013 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship]], where he won the bronze medal and was named to the All-Tournament Team,{{cite web|title=MVP PENO LEADS ALL TOURNAMENT TEAM|url=http://u16men.fibaeurope.com/en/coid_kG7Aj2BgG76iJfEHEBQN,2.articleMode_on.html|work=FIBAEurope.com|date=August 19, 2013|access-date=April 19, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160820141011/http://u16men.fibaeurope.com/en/coid_kG7Aj2BgG76iJfEHEBQN,2.articleMode_on.html|archive-date=August 20, 2016|url-status=dead}} after leading the tournament in blocks per game.{{cite web|title=FIBAEurope.com STATISTICAL LEADERS - PLAYERS Blocked Shots|url=https://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/statistics/p/rpp//tid/291/sid/9441/sp/ALL/ss/BL/srid/ALL/_/2013_U16_European_Championship_Men/player-leaders.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160814180736/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/statistics/p/rpp//tid/291/sid/9441/sp/ALL/ss/BL/srid/ALL/_/2013_U16_European_Championship_Men/player-leaders.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 14, 2016|work=FIBA.com|access-date=April 19, 2016}} Papagiannis also played at the [[2015 FIBA Under-19 World Championship|2015 FIBA Under-19 World Cup]], and the [[2015 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship]], where he was voted to the All-Tournament Team.{{cite web|title=MVP CHARALAMPOPOULOS HEADLINES ALL-STAR FIVE|url=http://u18men.fibaeurope.com/en/compID_8aYeHlfuGF-mF5IqO8aFH1.season_2015.roundID_11484.coid_AlTEzXTKH2wqmCeawxPWg1.articleMode_on.html|work=FIBAEurope.com|date=February 8, 2015|access-date=April 19, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150806035640/http://u18men.fibaeurope.com/en/compID_8aYeHlfuGF-mF5IqO8aFH1.season_2015.roundID_11484.coid_AlTEzXTKH2wqmCeawxPWg1.articleMode_on.html|archive-date=August 6, 2015|url-status=dead}} ===Greek senior national team=== [[File:Georgios Papagiannis 2017.jpg|thumb|250px|Papagiannis at the [[EuroBasket 2017]]]] Papagiannis became a member of the senior [[Greek national basketball team]] in 2017. He played with Greece at the [[EuroBasket 2017]], and at the [[2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup qualification (Europe)|2019 FIBA World Cup qualification]].
